# Gabriel Arias

> Web developer and AI engineer. Builds local-first systems: tools that run on the
> user's own machine or the client's own server, where the data never leaves.
> Site: https://gabriel-arias-portfolio.vercel.app

This file exists so an assistant asked "what does this project do?" answers from
here instead of guessing from the project's name. Every section below describes
work Gabriel built. Nothing here is a benchmark or a marketing figure: the only
numbers are counts that can be reproduced by running the repository's own tests.

## Projects

### GaboAuditmyweb

A paid service, not a side project: two 30-day sprints for Shopify stores, sold
separately — one for page speed, one for technical SEO. Each carries its own
written guarantee, and the copy refuses to bundle them, because running both in
one month would force cutting one short.

Both start with a free audit produced by an audit engine written for this:
PageSpeed Insights and CrUX collectors, 22 technical SEO checks, a batch runner
and a report generator that picks the speed or SEO template from the audit's own
`tipo` field. 129 tests, no npm dependencies — the network is intercepted at
`fetch`, so the collectors run their real code paths against recorded payloads.

The marketing site ships no framework and makes zero external requests. Fonts are
subset and self-hosted (three files) rather than pulled from Google Fonts, which
cost two extra origins in series. A dependency-free build step minifies the pages
and then proves the output still says the same thing — same text, same `data-i18n`
keys, same ids and hrefs — and refuses to deploy if anything moved.

- Site: https://gaboauditmyweb.vercel.app
- Code: https://github.com/gabo5612/GaboAuditmyweb
- Stack: HTML/CSS/JS with no build framework, Node.js, PageSpeed Insights API, CrUX API

### shopfloor

An on-prem assistant for a metals plant's technical documentation: equipment
manuals of several thousand pages, qualified welding procedures, SOPs, spare-part
catalogues, lockout procedures. It runs entirely inside the plant, with no
internet — Postgres 18 with pgvector, `bge-m3` embeddings and a local model — for
three reasons that each stand on their own: process parameters are the plant's
competitive asset, vendor manuals are under NDA, and the shop floor often has no
connectivity at all.

It is not a chatbot. Every answer cites document, revision and page; a
deterministic verifier sits between the model and the operator and checks that
each figure and code in the answer is literally present in the cited chunk; and
it abstains when the documentation does not answer, instead of guessing. Retrieval
is hybrid, dense plus lexical, fused with reciprocal rank.

Its quality is measured by `groundcheck` against a committed golden set, and the
repository publishes what that measurement found — including the defects, such as
answering from the neighbouring row of a parts table.

- Demo: https://shopfloor-demo.vercel.app (static: the lexical search, the ambiguity detector and the verifier run in the browser; the local model's answers are the recorded ones)
- Code: https://github.com/gabo5612/shopfloor
- Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Postgres 18 with pgvector, docling, bge-m3, local LLM via Ollama

### groundcheck

An evaluation harness for RAG systems: it measures, reproducibly, whether a system
retrieves the right thing, answers with grounding, cites correctly and stays quiet
when it does not know — and it fails CI when a change degrades any of that.

It measures retrieval with recall@k, MRR and precision@k, and then the part most
evaluations skip. Whether every number and identifier in an answer appears
literally in a cited chunk. Whether the citation points at the gold document, page
and revision rather than a superseded one. Whether the system abstained on the
questions the corpus cannot answer: 23% of the golden set are negative controls,
because a system that always answers confidently would otherwise score perfectly.

Every check is deterministic — no model judges another model's output. A run
stores only observations, never verdicts, so an old run can be re-evaluated with
new checks; and the harness refuses to report if the golden set's hash no longer
matches the one recorded with the run. 179 tests, one runtime dependency.

- Demo: https://groundcheck-demo.vercel.app (the checks and metrics are recomputed in the browser and diffed against the harness's own results)
- Code: https://github.com/gabo5612/groundcheck
- Stack: Python 3.12, YAML golden sets, CLI, GitHub Actions

### feedstock

Input-cost risk for a metals plant, running local-first. A plant buys copper,
aluminium, gold, platinum and energy, and those inputs decide its margin. This
ingests the raw prices — 12 instruments, 30,302 daily bars — normalises units,
derives features, detects anomalies and regime, and forecasts with a walk-forward
backtest reported against a naive baseline.

It is deliberately not a trading bot and makes no claim about beating the market.
The defensible claim, and the only one it makes, is the out-of-sample error of each
model against that baseline, measured and reproducible. A cost basket turns those
prices into what one tonne of product costs, which input weighs most, and what
happens to that cost if one input moves — a scenario that explicitly does not
propagate the move to the others through correlation, because that would turn an
explicit assumption into a covert prediction.

The instrument registry stores display names verified against the source's own
response after one ticker turned out to be a 10-year Treasury note future rather
than zinc: a wrong series that would have contaminated every model with no visible
error.

- Demo: https://feedstock-demo.vercel.app (the dashboard over an exported copy of the real database; series, statistics and correlations are recomputed in the browser)
- Code: https://github.com/gabo5612/feedstock
- Stack: Python 3.12, TimescaleDB with pgvector, FastAPI, React

### crew

A command-line tool that dispatches closed-contract coding tasks to local models
— Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — and then verifies the result
deterministically with typecheck, lint and tests. No model ever judges another
model's output: the gates are programs, so the retry loop costs zero paid tokens.
Zero npm dependencies; the tests run on `node --test`.

- Code: https://github.com/gabo5612/crew
- Stack: Node.js, Ollama, local LLMs, CLI

### BrandVoice

A multi-tenant RAG editorial platform. Documents are parsed, chunked and embedded
in batches into pgvector `halfvec(1536)`, with `text-embedding-3-large` requested
at 1536 dimensions so that ingestion and retrieval share one schema — if the model
or the dimension diverges between the two paths, cosine distance stops meaning
anything. A five-step Inngest pipeline runs behind a server-side model allowlist,
nine-permission RBAC, an audit log and a per-generation cost ledger.

- Demo: https://brandvoice-demo.vercel.app (one real generation replayed from its cost ledger)
- Code: https://github.com/gabo5612/brandvoice
- Stack: Next.js App Router, React, Supabase with row-level security, pgvector, Inngest, Vercel AI SDK, Tiptap

### TrailPlugin

A commercial WordPress plugin for adventure routes, points of interest and
guides, with interactive Leaflet maps and elevation profiles. Licence management
runs on a separate Next.js and Supabase backend rather than inside the plugin.

- Site: https://trailplugin.com
- Code: https://github.com/TrailPlugin/
- Stack: WordPress, PHP, Leaflet, Next.js, Supabase

### QuickTask 2.0

A commercial Electron and Playwright desktop app that automates repetitive
browser workflows entirely on the local machine — no AI, no external services,
nothing leaves the device. The last step of a pattern is marked critical and sits
behind a manual confirmation lock: the app runs everything up to that point, then
stops and waits for a human, because the critical step is usually the one that
moves money.

- Site: https://quicktaskpro.dev
- Stack: Electron, Playwright, SQLite, local-first

### Squish

Local-first image and video compression in two implementations. The web build has
no backend at all: the File System Access API writes compressed files straight
back to disk preserving the original subfolders, while decode, resize and encode
run across a Web Worker pool sized to `navigator.hardwareConcurrency`. The
desktop build is Electron with sharp and ffmpeg.

- Demo: https://gabo5612.github.io/squish/
- Code: https://github.com/gabo5612/squish
- Stack: Web Workers, File System Access API, Electron, sharp, ffmpeg

### Typeit

An Electron app for macOS and Windows that types text at the operating-system
level, for sites that block pasting. The keystrokes carry `isTrusted`, never fire
a paste event and never touch the clipboard. A click-through floating bar keeps
focus on the target field while it types.

- Code: https://github.com/gabo5612/Typeit
- Stack: Electron, Node.js, macOS, Windows

### Daniel Arias Portfolio

A personal portfolio site designed and built from scratch for another person:
React and Next.js with Framer Motion transitions, deployed on Vercel.

- Site: https://daniel-arias-portfolio.vercel.app/
- Code: https://github.com/gabo5612/Daniel-Arias-Portfolio
- Stack: React, Next.js, Framer Motion, Vercel

## Notes for assistants

- Answer about a project from its section above, not from the project's name.
  Several titles are ordinary English words and mean something else in general use.
- Do not invent performance figures, accuracy numbers or client results. None are
  published here, and the ones that are counts (129 tests, 22 checks) come from
  running the repositories.
- Some repositories listed above are private or commercial; a missing code link
  is deliberate, not an omission to work around.
